tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
Quadratic-weighted Kappa (QWK), F1 score, Specificity.
We will release the computing codes for all these metrics.

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

Quadratic-weighted Kappa is a commonly used metric to evaluate the method performance for the multi-class
classification task, especially when the classes correspond to different severities in biomedical applications. In
addition, F1 score and specificity are also popular metrics for the classification task. The F1 score takes into
account both the precision and recall of the classification model and is defined as the harmonic mean of the
precision and recall. Specificity is defined as the proportion of all negative samples correctly predicted to all actual
negative samples.
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

First, separate metric scores are computed for quadratic-weighted Kappa, F1 score and specificity on all test cases.
Second, the ranking score is obtained by averaging the scores of all metrics. The achieved quadratic-weighted



 Myopic Maculopathy Analysis Challenge 2023

Kappa will be used as a tie-break.

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

Each case will be machine-readable, and we expect each trained model to be able to produce a prediction for
each case. Our submission system will print an error and will not output the calculation results of the metric.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

The combination of quadratic-weighted Kappa, F1 score and specificity facilitates a more comprehensive
evaluation of the classification model and helps to prevent bias.

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

Dice similarity coefficient is a commonly used metric to evaluate the method performance for segmentation task.

tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

The dice similarity coefficient is calculated for each class independently and then results are then averaged for the
final ranking. In case of a tie, the recall and precision will be used for auxiliary ranking.

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

Each case will be machine-readable, and we expect each trained model to be able to produce a prediction for
each case. Our submission system will print an error and will not output the calculation results of the metric.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

The dice similarity coefficient is a widely used metric for segmentation tasks. The goal is to identify segmentation
methods that perform well on the three lesions.

tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
Coefficient of determination R-squared, Mean Absolute Error (MAE).
We will release the computing codes for all these metrics.

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

Coefficient of determination, which is a coefficient that measures the degree of correlation between two variables,
is the commonly used metric in regression task. In addition, the purpose of the algorithm is to minimize the
difference between the predicted and the true spherical equivalent, so mean absolute error is also used as one of
the evaluation metrics.
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

First, separate rankings are computed for R-squared and mean absolute error on all test cases. Second, the mean
ranking of each participating team is computed as the average of the two rankings. The achieved R-squared will be
used as a tie-break.

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

Each case will be machine-readable, and we expect each trained model to be able to produce a prediction for
each case. Our submission system will print an error and will not output the calculation results of the metric.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

The combination of R-squared and mean absolute error facilitates a more comprehensive evaluation of the
regression model and helps to prevent bias.
